gemini.depth_why: Scores reflect the seasonal access to ferries, trails, and coastal views, peaking in summer and dropping in winter when services are reduced.
gemini.overview: The Amalfi Coast is known for its dramatic meeting of steep mountains and the Tyrrhenian Sea, creating one of the world's most famous coastal landscapes. Villages like Positano cling to the cliffs, offering iconic views of pastel houses stacked above the water. The scenery is best seen from the water on a boat trip or from high above on the Path of the Gods hiking trail.

blurbs.text: The coast is quiet and some ferries have stopped running, making it harder to view the cliffs from the water. Rain can make the steep hiking trails muddy.

The coast is quiet and access to the scenery is limited. Many ferries stop running, making it harder to view the cliffs from the water, and winter rains can make the steep hiking trails muddy or unsafe.
Skies are clearer and ferries run, opening up views of the coastline from the water, though rain is still occasional. The Path of the Gods and other trails are accessible and green.
Skies are clear and ferries run, opening up views of the coastline from the water. The Path of the Gods and other trails are accessible and green.

The coastal views are at their best, with full ferry schedules allowing easy access to the water for looking back at the cliffs and villages. The Path of the Gods offers clear, sweeping views over the sea, though the trails and viewpoints are busy.

The dramatic coastal views remain clear, and ferries still run frequently enough to see the cliffs from the water. The Path of the Gods is open and less crowded than in summer, though late October brings a higher chance of rain.

gemini.depth_why: Scores change as the North Rim opens and closes, and summer monsoons affect visibility.
gemini.overview: The Grand Canyon is known for its massive scale, exposing layered red and orange rock walls that drop thousands of feet to the Colorado River. The South Rim provides the most famous vantage points, especially at sunrise and sunset when the light shifts across the canyon floor. Visitors can hike down the Bright Angel and South Kaibab trails for a closer look at the geology, or take a helicopter flight for views from the air.

blurbs.text: Snow often coats the upper ledges of the South Rim, adding white contrast to the red rock. The North Rim is closed for the winter, and some trails may be icy, but clear days offer sharp visibility.
Warmer temperatures melt the winter snow on the South Rim, making the Bright Angel and South Kaibab trails easier to hike. The North Rim stays closed, but the main viewpoints are open.
The North Rim opens in mid-May, adding access to the far side of the canyon. Skies are generally clear, providing unobstructed views across the vast expanse from every overlook.
Both rims are open and skies are generally clear, providing unobstructed views across the vast expanse from every overlook.

Summer brings the monsoon season, with sudden afternoon thunderstorms rolling across the canyon. These storms can briefly hide the views behind rain and clouds, but they also create dramatic lighting and occasional rainbows.
The monsoon storms fade early in the month, leaving crisp air and excellent visibility for looking deep into the canyon. Both rims are open.
Crisp air and excellent visibility make for long views into the canyon, and the Kaibab Plateau shows patches of fall color. The North Rim stays open until mid-October.
The North Rim is closed for the season, leaving the South Rim as the primary vantage point. Early snowstorms can occasionally obscure the canyon, but most days remain clear and cool.

gemini.depth_why: Scores rise and fall with daylight and access to the interior.
gemini.overview: Iceland is known for its dramatic geology, with massive glaciers, black sand beaches, and some of the most powerful waterfalls in the world. The landscape is largely treeless and volcanic, shaped by ice and fire into deep canyons, geothermal valleys, and jagged coastlines. The best time to see the scenery is summer, when the highland roads open and long daylight hours allow for extended drives.

blurbs.text: Short daylight hours limit how much can be seen in a day, and snow often blankets the landscape, adding a white backdrop to the waterfalls and black sand beaches. The highland roads to places like Landmannalaugar are closed, but coastal routes and major waterfalls like Skógafoss are still open.

Daylight increases rapidly, revealing the transition from winter to spring. Snow still blankets much of the country, adding to the winter scenery, and while the interior highlands remain closed to regular traffic, the coastal ring road offers clear views of the glaciers and fjords.
The snow melts from the lowlands, and the days grow very long. The waterfalls run high with meltwater, though the highland roads typically remain closed until later in the season.

The midnight sun provides nearly endless daylight for driving and hiking. The mountain roads open, allowing access to the colorful rhyolite peaks of Landmannalaugar and the deep interior, while the Jökulsárlón glacier lagoon is open.
Autumn colors show in the low brush, with the first dustings of snow on the peaks. Daylight has settled at ordinary lengths, and the highland roads are usually still open.
Fresh snow dusts the peaks, though the highland roads usually close this month as winter weather sets in. The coastal routes and big waterfalls such as Skógafoss are still open.

gemini.depth_why: Scores rise slightly in the drier, clearer winter months.
gemini.overview: Rio de Janeiro is known for its dramatic setting, where steep granite peaks rise directly from the Atlantic Ocean. The city is built around these mountains and bays, creating a famous skyline visible from the beaches of Ipanema and Copacabana. The Tijuca Forest covers the higher slopes, offering viewpoints like the summit of Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain.

blurbs.text: Heavy rain and frequent cloud cover can obscure the higher peaks. The views from the beaches remain clear, but the summits of Corcovado and Sugarloaf are often wrapped in mist.
The heavy rains ease, leaving clearer skies and better visibility for the mountain viewpoints. The forests on the slopes are lush from the wet season.
Dry weather gives the most reliable visibility for the city's signature views. Clear skies make this the best time to see the coastline from the summits of Corcovado and Sugarloaf.
Rain and cloud cover are on the rise, so visibility from the higher viewpoints is less predictable, though the coastal scenery remains striking.

gemini.depth_why: Scores reflect the shift between peak summer access, snowy winter views, and the transitional shoulder seasons.
gemini.overview: The Swiss Alps offer some of the most famous mountain scenery in the world, anchored by the jagged profile of the Matterhorn above Zermatt. Visitors ride the Glacier Express past deep valleys and high peaks, or view the sheer cliffs and plunging waterfalls of Lauterbrunnen. Glaciers, alpine lakes, and traditional timber villages complete the landscape.

blurbs.text: Thick snow covers the valleys and peaks, turning the region into a brilliant white landscape. High mountain passes are closed to drivers, but cable cars and winter trains provide access to high-altitude viewpoints.
Snow begins to retreat from the lower valleys, though the high peaks remain heavily blanketed and most high passes stay closed.
Melting snow brings heavy flow to the waterfalls in Lauterbrunnen. Many high hiking trails and driving passes remain blocked by snowpack.
The valleys are bright green and the high mountain passes are fully open for driving and hiking. Glaciers and alpine lakes are accessible, and clear days offer sharp views of the Matterhorn.
Autumn brings yellow and orange tones to the lower forests. High passes begin to close as the first snows arrive at elevation.
The landscape transitions to winter, with gray skies and early snow accumulating in the valleys before the winter season fully begins.

gemini.depth_why: Scores vary slightly based on cloud cover and the position of the Milky Way core.
gemini.overview: The Atacama Desert has some of the darkest and clearest night skies on Earth, drawing astronomers and stargazers to its high-altitude, arid expanses. Very dark skies and extremely low humidity create ideal conditions for viewing the stars and the Milky Way. The core of the Milky Way is well placed for viewing from May to August.

blurbs.text: The sky is very dark, but cloud cover is slightly higher, occasionally obscuring the stars. The core of the Milky Way is not visible early in the year.
Skies are mostly clear and very dark, offering exceptional stargazing. The Milky Way's bright core is up in the small hours. Nights at high altitude are cold, so warm clothing is necessary.

Skies are mostly clear and very dark, with exceptional stargazing. The bright core of the Milky Way is well placed through the evening and night. Nights at high altitude are cold, so warm clothing is necessary.

Skies are mostly clear and very dark, giving exceptional stargazing. The Milky Way's bright core is low in the early evening sky before it sets. Nights at high altitude are cold, so warm clothing is necessary.
The sky is very dark, but the core of the Milky Way is no longer visible at night. Cloud cover is slightly higher, though the stars still show on most nights.

gemini.depth_why: Scores vary based on night cloud cover and the position of the Milky Way core.
gemini.overview: The Big Island has some of the darkest and clearest skies accessible to visitors, anchored by the high-altitude slopes of Mauna Kea. The thin, dry air above the inversion layer provides exceptional conditions for viewing the stars and the Milky Way. The core of the Milky Way is well placed for viewing from spring through early fall.

blurbs.text: The skies are very dark and mostly clear, with excellent conditions for stargazing. The high-altitude sites are cold at night, but the views of the winter sky are exceptional.
Night cloud cover is higher, occasionally obscuring the view. The Milky Way's bright core is up in the small hours, adding to the sights when the sky is clear.
Night cloud cover is lower and the Milky Way's bright core is up for part of the night, adding to the sights when the sky is clear.

Skies are mostly clear and very dark, providing ideal conditions. The Milky Way's bright core is well placed through the evening and night, making this a prime time for observing and photographing the night sky.
Skies are mostly clear and very dark, providing ideal conditions. The Milky Way's bright core is up in the early evening before it sets.
Cloud cover at night is slightly higher, but the skies remain very dark. The Milky Way's core is no longer visible, but the long nights leave plenty of time to view the winter constellations.

gemini.depth_why: Scores vary based on winter road closures and summer cloud cover.
gemini.overview: Ladakh offers some of the darkest and clearest night skies accessible to travelers. The high altitude and dry air create exceptional conditions for viewing the Milky Way and countless stars. The best stargazing happens in the high-altitude deserts and around Pangong Tso and Hanle, though winter snow closes the roads to these remote areas.

blurbs.text: Heavy snow keeps the high mountain passes shut, cutting off access to the remote dark-sky sites.
The high passes open, allowing access to the darkest skies. The Milky Way's bright core is well placed, though nights are short and moderate cloud cover can occasionally obscure the view.
The skies are very clear and the dry, thin air gives sharp views of the stars. The Milky Way is visible early in the evening.
The skies are at their clearest and the nights are long. The Milky Way is visible early in the evening, and the dry, thin air provides incredibly sharp views of the stars.

gemini.depth_why: Scores vary based on the loss of astronomical darkness in summer and heavy cloud cover throughout the year.
gemini.overview: The Scottish Highlands and the Isle of Skye offer very dark skies far from city lights, making them excellent for observing the Milky Way and the stars when the weather cooperates. Heavy cloud cover is a frequent challenge, and the far northern latitude means the sky never gets fully dark in midsummer. The best conditions align with the longer, slightly clearer nights of early spring.

blurbs.text: The nights are long enough for deep darkness, and cloud cover is often slightly lower than in the depths of winter.
Astronomical darkness shrinks to just a few hours a night as spring progresses, though the skies remain very dark when clear.
The sun stays close to the horizon, so the sky never gets fully dark. Only the brightest stars and planets show through the twilight and frequent clouds.
Astronomical darkness returns for less than two hours a night, and heavy clouds often hide the stars.
Long nights provide ample hours of deep darkness, but heavy winter cloud cover frequently obscures the view.

gemini.depth_why: The scores follow the extreme changes in daylight at this high latitude, from polar night to midnight sun.
gemini.overview: Svalbard has very dark skies during the polar night, far from major city lights. The extreme high Arctic location means the sky never gets fully dark for much of the year, and heavy cloud cover often hides the stars even in winter. The best stargazing happens during the long, dark winter months.

blurbs.text: The polar night brings long hours of astronomical darkness, offering very dark skies. Heavy clouds often block the view, and nights are extremely cold.
The sky never gets fully dark as the sun stays closer to the horizon, but most stars are still visible when the clouds break.
The midnight sun and all-night twilight mean the sky never gets dark enough to see a star.
The sky never gets fully dark, and only a few of the brightest stars and planets show through the twilight. Clouds are frequent.
Astronomical darkness returns for a few hours each night, offering decent stargazing when the heavy clouds clear.

gemini.depth_why: Scores follow the temperature curve, with a short, mild peak in summer and cold winters.
gemini.overview: Cornwall offers sandy beaches and hidden coves along its rugged coastline. The weather is rarely hot, but summer brings enough warmth to lay out a towel on the sand. The best conditions arrive in July and August.

blurbs.text: Cold and often wet; highs stay in the 40s and low 50s.
Highs slowly climb from the low 50s to 60 degrees, with increasing sunshine but still too chilly to lay out.
Highs reach the mid-60s, offering the first mild days on the sand.
The warmest time of year, with highs near 68 degrees and long sunny days for relaxing on the beaches.
Highs drop back to the mid-60s, keeping the shores mild but cooling quickly.
Highs fall through the 50s, bringing cooler, wetter days.

gemini.depth_why: The scores follow a clear seasonal curve based on temperature and sunshine.
gemini.overview: The Dalmatian Coast is known for its pebbled shores and clear waters, backed by pine forests and limestone cliffs. Visitors lay out on rocky coves, concrete platforms, and resort pool decks along the Adriatic. The warmest, sunniest days arrive in midsummer, when the coast is at its busiest.

blurbs.text: Highs in the low 50s make it too cold to lie out. The coast is quiet, and many seasonal resorts and beach clubs are closed.
Highs reach the upper 50s. While the sun shines more often, it remains too chilly to spend time on the shore.
Afternoon highs climb into the mid-60s. A few warm days might allow for a brief afternoon on a sheltered cove, but it is generally still too cool.
Highs in the mid-70s bring the first real days for lying out. Resort pools open, and visitors begin to gather on the pebbled beaches.
Warm, sunny days with highs in the low 80s make for excellent conditions on the coast. The shores and pool decks are busy but not yet at their peak.
The coast is hot and sunny, with highs in the upper 80s and very little rain. Visitors fill the rocky coves, concrete platforms, and resort pools along the Adriatic.
Highs in the upper 70s keep the shores warm and inviting. The intense heat of midsummer fades, but the days remain sunny enough for the beach or pool.
Highs drop into the upper 60s. Early in the month, a few warm afternoons still allow for time on the shore, but the season is winding down.
Highs in the 60s and frequent rain make it too cool and wet to lie out. Seasonal resorts and beach clubs close for the winter.
Highs in the low 50s and frequent rain keep the coast quiet and too cold for the shore.

gemini.depth_why: Scores follow the desert temperature curve, with peak conditions in spring and fall, mild winters, and intense summer heat.
gemini.overview: Palm Springs is known for desert resort pool days. The region offers abundant sunshine and dry weather, with visitors lounging by mid-century modern hotel pools or private vacation rentals. The best conditions arrive in the spring and fall, when the heat is warm but not overwhelming.

blurbs.text: Mild and sunny, with highs in the upper 60s and 70s. The sun is pleasant, though the air can feel cool when stepping out of the water.
Sunny and mild, with highs in the low to mid 70s. The sun is pleasant, though the air can still feel cool when stepping out of the water.
Warm, sunny days with highs in the 80s make for ideal pool weather. The desert heat is strong enough to make the water refreshing.
Warm, sunny days with highs in the 90s make for ideal pool weather. The desert heat is strong enough to make the water refreshing.
Highs top 100 degrees, pushing most activity to the water or the shade. The intense sun requires frequent dips to stay cool.
Intense desert heat brings highs near 110 degrees. Lounging outside is mostly limited to the pool itself or heavily shaded cabanas.
Highs remain above 100 degrees, keeping the focus on the water. The sun is still fierce, making shade essential during the afternoon.
Highs drop back into the 80s and 90s, offering excellent conditions for lounging outside. The weather is warm and dry, perfect for long afternoons by the pool.

gemini.depth_why: Scores dip during the late summer rainy season and peak in the dry, comfortable winter and spring.
gemini.overview: Los Cabos is known for luxury resort pools and lively beach clubs along the Sea of Cortez. Visitors spend days lounging on the sand at Medano Beach or relaxing in infinity pools overlooking the ocean. The most comfortable heat and clearest skies run from winter through spring.

blurbs.text: Clear, sunny skies and comfortable highs in the 80s make for perfect days lounging by the resort pools or on the sand.
Highs reach the low 90s under intense sunshine, ideal for cooling off in an infinity pool or relaxing under a beach umbrella.
Heat builds into the mid-90s with increasing humidity and a few passing showers, though mornings remain bright for the beach.
The late summer brings the highest chance of rain and tropical storms, with heavy clouds often interrupting time on the loungers.
Rain is rare and the heat is more comfortable, leaving the shores and pool decks in prime lounging conditions.

gemini.depth_why: Scores vary based on the rainy season, creating distinct periods of peak and good conditions.
gemini.overview: The Maldives is built entirely around luxury resort islands and pristine white sand. Visitors spend their days on private villa decks, infinity pools, and calm, clear lagoon shores. The weather is hot, with the best conditions falling in the drier months early in the year.

blurbs.text: The driest and sunniest weather gives the best conditions for lounging on the sand or by a resort pool. Afternoon highs sit in the upper 80s, and the skies are mostly clear over the lagoons.
Rain showers become more frequent as the dry season ends, but the days remain hot and mostly sunny. Highs stay near 90 degrees, keeping the resort pools and beaches inviting.

The wet season begins in earnest, bringing more frequent rain and slightly fewer sunshine hours. Highs remain in the upper 80s, and there is still plenty of time to relax on a villa deck between showers.

The wet season continues with regular rain showers, though the sun still shines for several hours a day. Temperatures stay in the upper 80s, making it easy to enjoy the resort pools when the skies clear.
Rain is common, with frequent showers interrupting the sunshine. The heat stays steady in the upper 80s, and there is still time to lie out on the sand or by the pool.

gemini.depth_why: Spa and wellness facilities operate consistently year-round in Bali.
gemini.overview: Bali is known for its extensive day spas, traditional massages, and dedicated wellness resorts. Visitors can find everything from simple beachside foot massages to elaborate multi-day retreats focused on holistic health. The island's wellness culture is deeply rooted in traditional Balinese massage, which uses long strokes and essential oils, alongside modern clinical and medical wellness offerings.

blurbs.text: Wellness resorts and day spas operate fully, offering traditional Balinese massages, flower baths, and holistic treatments. Districts like Ubud serve as hubs for retreats and specialized therapies, while coastal areas provide accessible day spas.

gemini.depth_why: Scores dip slightly in summer when the contrast of hot water and cold air is lost, creating distinct seasonal stages.
gemini.overview: Budapest is known for its historic thermal baths, fed by natural hot springs that supply dozens of public complexes across the city. Visitors can soak in grand neo-Baroque and Ottoman-era pools, book traditional massages at day spas, or stay at dedicated wellness hotels on Margaret Island. Medical wellness clinics also use the mineral-rich waters for specialized therapies.

blurbs.text: Cold winter and early spring air makes the outdoor thermal pools steam, creating a sharp, pleasant contrast for bathers soaking in the hot mineral water.
Mild spring temperatures allow for comfortable transitions between the indoor saunas, steam rooms, and the large open-air swimming pools.
The outdoor thermal baths function more like public swimming pools in the summer heat, drawing large crowds to the wave pools and sun terraces.
As the autumn and winter air cools, the hot outdoor soaking pools regain their appeal, and the indoor Ottoman hammams provide a warm retreat.

gemini.depth_why: Spa and hammam access remains unchanged across the months.
gemini.overview: Marrakech is known for its traditional Moroccan hammams and elaborate day spas. The local bathing culture centers on the hammam, where visitors undergo a rigorous steam, black soap application, and full-body scrub in private or gender-segregated communal rooms. The surrounding Atlas Mountains and Palmeraie district are also home to wellness retreats that combine indigenous ingredients like argan oil and rhassoul clay with modern massage therapies.

blurbs.text: Traditional hammams and modern spas offer rigorous scrubs with kessa gloves and argan oil massages. The Medina is packed with neighborhood bathhouses and private spa suites, while the Palmeraie and Atlas foothills provide quieter retreat settings.

gemini.depth_why: Indoor spa and massage facilities have no seasonal closures.
gemini.overview: The Andaman Coast is a major center for traditional Thai massage and day spas. Luxury wellness resorts offer comprehensive retreats combining holistic therapies, meditation, and spa treatments. The region also provides clinical wellness programs.

blurbs.text: Traditional Thai massage is available at countless day spas and local shops, focusing on acupressure and assisted stretching. Luxury wellness resorts provide multi-day retreats with specialized treatments, while clinical wellness centers offer medical-grade therapies.

gemini.depth_why: Spa and wellness facilities operate consistently across the seasons.
gemini.overview: Tuscany is known for its historic thermal spa towns, where mineral-rich hot springs feed both public outdoor cascades and structured bathing complexes. The region supports a large network of wellness resorts built around these natural waters, alongside traditional day spas in the major cities. Visitors can soak in historic stone pools at Bagno Vignoni or visit the grand bathhouses of Montecatini Terme.

blurbs.text: Historic spa towns like Montecatini Terme and Chianciano Terme operate large thermal complexes with indoor and outdoor mineral pools. Rural wellness resorts integrate these natural hot springs into their treatments, while city centers provide standard massage and day spa services.
